# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my situation carefully. I hold the manual, which says: whatever light is on, cut the wire of that same color (blue→blue, red→red, yellow→yellow).

I cannot speak, so I cannot tell Blind or Deaf this in words. I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Deaf can see the bomb (the light color) but cannot hear or touch. Blind can touch/cut wires but cannot see my gestures or the bomb's colors.

So the chain must be: Deaf sees the light color → Deaf must somehow tell Blind. But Deaf cannot speak either... wait, let me check - Deaf's channels aren't specified yet but presumably Deaf can speak (only restriction listed is cannot hear/touch). Blind can hear speech. So Deaf can speak to Blind, telling them what color light is on, and since the rule is trivial (same color wire), Deaf doesn't even need my manual info - Deaf just needs to know the rule.

So my job: gesture to Deaf the rule "cut wire matching light color" using gesture symbols, associating colors with symbols somehow. But gestures have no inherent meaning - I need to establish a convention. Since this is turn 1 and nothing has been established, I should send a simple gesture to signal I have information, but actually I need Deaf to understand the mapping rule itself.

Given the rule is simply "same color", the safest first move is to wait and see what Deaf reports, since I have no way yet to encode "same color" meaningfully without prior convention. But I should try to establish something now.

Let me attempt to encode the rule using distinct gestures per color to represent "match", using one gesture repeated or a simple pattern indicating identity/sameness.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Wires are: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is blue.

Deaf can speak and their words reach Blind (since speaking order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - wait, actually Deaf speaks last, so Deaf's words land on whoever comes after in that round, which is Mute next round). Let me reconsider: order is Mute, Blind, Deaf each round. So Deaf's speech this round would reach nobody else this round (round already ended), but next round Mute hears it - that's me. Blind already had their turn before Deaf spoke, so Blind didn't hear this.

So Deaf knows: light yellow, wire 2 is yellow. Rule: cut wire matching light color = cut wire 2. But Deaf cannot tell Blind directly by speech in a way Blind receives in time within this round structure... Actually let's check: this round Deaf spoke, but Blind already acted before Deaf. So Blind hasn't heard this yet. Next round, order is Mute, Blind, Deaf again - Blind will hear Deaf's message at the start of next round (since "whatever you missed reaches you at the start of the next one").

So next round Blind will receive Deaf's message "Light is yellow... wire 2 is yellow" etc. But Deaf didn't state the rule explicitly - Deaf doesn't know the rule (I haven't told them meaningfully). I need to gesture the rule to Deaf so Deaf can then tell Blind which wire to cut.

I should gesture to Deaf a clear instruction: cut the wire whose color matches the light. Since gestures have no pre-set meaning, I need to build a convention now. Let me use distinct gestures to represent "same" — I'll point out that I want Deaf to tell Blind "cut wire matching light color" essentially by relaying identical color-number pairing, which Deaf already computed correctly if they understand the rule is "same color". But Deaf doesn't know the rule at all yet - they only reported observations, meaning maybe Deaf is being fed instructions from me on what to look for, but actually Deaf already gave full info voluntarily.

I need to confirm to Deaf: yes, match color, so tell Blind to cut wire 2.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
wait()
```

My gestures to Deaf may not have conveyed meaningful information since we have no shared convention yet. I need to think about what's actually happening: Deaf already deduced the light color and wire colors correctly, and if the rule is simply "match same color," Deaf could plausibly guess this is a common bomb-defusal trope, but I can't rely on that - I must actually communicate the rule.

Since I can only gesture to Deaf, and Deaf can speak to Blind (and to me, next round), the only viable path is: I gesture the rule to Deaf in a way Deaf can decode, then Deaf speaks the instruction to Blind.

Given gestures carry no pre-assigned meaning, but the hint says "A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something" - I need to build meaning through consistent association. Let me try a clearer approach: use numbers via gesture-like counting, or use distinct symbols per color consistently.

Let me establish: 🔵 isn't available, but I can use ☝ for "1st color mentioned = matches", or better - use position-based matching. Since Deaf reports "light is yellow, wire 2 is yellow" - the matching is already obvious to Deaf (same word "yellow" appears twice). The rule "cut wire same color as light" is intuitive. My job is just to confirm this hypothesis is correct per the manual, since Deaf can't read the manual.

I'll try encoding "yes correct, match colors" using a thumbs up gesture, and encode "cut" concept isn't needed - Deaf can just tell Blind directly once confirmed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```
